description: Hi! I'm Ayuub Duba, a full-stack developer and UI designer from Kenya with a passion for space science, astrophysics, and building real-time interactive tools. My core stack includes React, Vite, Node.js, and Python, with hands-on experience!
summary:
AURORA is a real-time space weather command dashboard built to monitor solar activity and forecast geomagnetic storm impacts before they strike Earth made By Ayuub. Severe solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) pose major risks to satellites, GPS navigation, aviation, and power grid infrastructure, yet raw space weather telemetry is often difficult for operators to visualize and model quickly.

By integrating live data from official NASA DONKI API endpoints with a physics-backed Interplanetary Drag-Based Model (DBM) simulator, AURORA calculates CME propagation speeds, deceleration profiles, and estimated Earth arrival times in real time. Presented through a sleek, tactical dark-mode interface, AURORA empowers satellite operators, researchers, and emergency planners with rapid situational awareness and actionable forecasting during high-risk solar weather events.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

AURORA is a unified, hyper-local Multi-Hazard Early Warning & Farm Resilience Command platform that bridges orbital satellite telemetry with ground-level community alerts. Users drop a pin on their farm, village, or infrastructure site to generate a real-time, four-light risk status card and interactive map overlay covering four critical environmental hazards:

1. Drought Monitoring: Combines NASA SMAP root-zone soil moisture data with NASA GPM IMERG precipitation feeds to advise farmers on optimal planting and irrigation windows.

2. Wildfire Detection: Fuses near-real-time NASA FIRMS thermal hotspot detections with live ground-truth telemetry from local ESP32 sensor nodes (measuring ambient temperature and smoke density) to catch fires early.

3. Flood Risk Modeling: Overlays GPM IMERG rainfall forecasts onto NASA SRTM digital elevation models to identify low-lying terrain vulnerable to runoff and flash flooding.

4. Space Weather Alerts: Integrates live NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) geomagnetic storm feeds into a non-intrusive status banner warning of potential GPS/GNSS degradation, HF radio blackouts, or power grid disruptions.

When any threshold is breached, AURORA automatically translates the technical telemetry into plain-language, actionable warnings delivered directly to residents via WhatsApp and SMS (e.g., "Heavy rain expected in 48 hours—avoid planting in the low field").

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Smallholder farmers and rural communities—such as those across Machakos County, Kenya—frequently face overlapping climate and environmental hazards, yet raw satellite datasets are fragmented and inaccessible to non-specialists. AURORA democratizes NASA Earth and Space science by turning complex multi-spectral data into simple, life- and livelihood-saving decisions on basic mobile phones. Its intended impact is to reduce crop losses from poorly timed planting or unpredicted floods, accelerate wildfire response before blazes spread, and safeguard precision agriculture and local infrastructure during geomagnetic storms.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used:

- Frontend & Mapping: React, Vite, JavaScript/TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet.js for interactive multi-layer geospatial visualization.

- Backend & Data Pipeline: Node.js/Express and Python services that poll, normalize, and cache geospatial feeds from NASA SMAP, GPM IMERG, NASA FIRMS, SRTM, and NOAA SWPC.

- IoT Hardware & Messaging: ESP32 microcontrollers equipped with smoke, temperature, and capacitive soil moisture sensors streaming real-time telemetry over MQTT, paired with WhatsApp/SMS webhook automation for instant mobile alerting.

- Deployment & Version Control: GitHub, Netlify, and VS Code.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

Rather than building separate, siloed tools for agriculture, disaster response, and space weather, AURORA unifies Earth observation and heliophysics into a single intuitive "four-light risk card" paired with hybrid satellite-to-ground verification. Key factors considered during development included last-mile accessibility (delivering plain-language SMS/WhatsApp alerts so end users do not need high-end smartphones or scientific training), low-latency data caching for regions with intermittent internet connectivity, and modular hardware integration so communities can deploy affordable ESP32 ground nodes alongside free NASA orbital data.
